name: Unison
title: Unison (M5b)

type.text: **Algebraic data types with exhaustive pattern matching**: Like Haskell, separates cases explicitly
**Abilities (algebraic effects)**: Superior to monads for separating different effect types
**Content-addressed functions decouple code from names**: Functions identified by hash of their implementation
**Structural typing for abilities**: Can satisfy ability requirements without explicit declarations
**No orphan instances**: Type classes (abilities) prevent distant coupling
**Distributed computing primitives**: `Remote` ability separates local from distributed concerns

construction.text: **Immutable data structures by default**: No coupling through mutation
**Smart constructors via abilities**: Construction effects tracked in type system
**No global state**: Pure functions can't have hidden dependencies
**Content addressing eliminates initialization order**: Functions self-contained, no module load order coupling

memory.text: **Runtime GC decouples memory**: No manual memory management
**Immutability prevents reference cycles**: Simpler GC, fewer leaks
**Distributed execution abstracts memory**: `Remote` computation handles serialization automatically
**GC implementation details not public**: Couples performance to runtime implementation

error.text: **Abilities make errors explicit**: `{Exception} Result` shows failure in type signature
**Algebraic effects compose**: Can combine error handling with other effects naturally
**Pattern matching on Either/Result**: Exhaustiveness checking prevents missed error paths
**No unchecked exceptions**: All failure modes visible in types

concurrency.text: **Distributed computing built-in**: Functions can execute remotely without changing logic
**Content addressing enables safe deployment**: Update function implementation without breaking callers
**Abilities separate concurrent operations**: `Concurrent`, `Remote` abilities explicit in signatures
**Deterministic execution**: Pure functions compose regardless of execution location

platform.text: **Own runtime, no foreign VM**: Unison ships its own runtime, so programs target no third-party virtual machine such as the JVM or the CLR
**Native binaries for the desktop platforms**: UCM ships for macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon), 64-bit Linux, and Windows
**Cloud is optional**: A local codebase builds, tests, and runs with `ucm` alone; Unison Cloud and Unison Share are services you may adopt, not platform prerequisites
**Host-independent code identity**: Because definitions are identified by a hash, a codebase binds to no filesystem layout or machine-specific package registry

performance.text: **Own runtime**: Predictable performance, its own runtime avoids JVM dependency
**Distributed execution**: Can distribute computation across machines transparently
**GC pauses**: Unison's own runtime collects garbage, so pauses are non-deterministic
**Persistent data structures overhead**: Immutability couples performance to structure sharing
**Network abstraction cost**: `Remote` computation couples performance to serialization/network

ecosystem.text: **Very small ecosystem**: Limited library availability couples a project to manual implementation or to the few libraries that exist
**Codebase Manager is innovative**: Content addressing decouples from traditional VCS
**Excellent error messages**: Compiler feedback decouples debugging from trial-and-error
**UCM learning curve**: Novel workflow couples productivity to understanding new paradigm
**Share functionality built-in**: Can publish/consume code via Unison Share without separate package manager

evolution.text: **Content addressing handles refactoring**: Rename functions without breaking dependents (they reference by hash)
**Upgrade functions independently**: Can use multiple versions of same function (different hashes)
**Pre-1.0 stability**: Breaking changes still occur while the language evolves, coupling code to a language version
**Automatic migration tools**: UCM helps update codebases when language changes
**Small team**: Development pace couples to limited resources

domain.text: **Excellent for distributed systems**: Built-in remote execution separates logic from distribution
**Strong for backend services**: Type safety + distributed primitives
**Immature for production**: Ecosystem couples adoption to risk tolerance
**Great for exploratory programming**: Content addressing enables fearless refactoring

learning.text: **Novel paradigm**: Content addressing + abilities + UCM workflow all new concepts
**Good documentation**: Unison docs and tour explain concepts well
**Requires functional thinking**: Learning couples to FP background
**UCM workflow different**: Codebase management couples to unlearning Git habits and to understanding content addressing

syntax.text: **UCM commands**: Learning curve for codebase operations
**Hash-qualified names optional**: Can use readable names, hashes only when needed

testing.text: **Watch expressions**: Can add tests directly in code files
**Pure functions easy to test**: No hidden state coupling
**Property testing support**: Can write generative tests
**Debugging tools immature**: Stack traces couple to runtime implementation
**Distributed debugging hard**: Remote computation couples debugging to network

security.text: **Type safety**: No null, no type confusion
**Content addressing**: Function identity verified by hash, prevents tampering
**Ability system**: Can control what effects functions perform
**Distributed execution risk**: Remote computation couples security to network trust

governance.text: **Semantics rest on the reference implementation**: the published specification defines the language as the reference implementation behaves, and no conformance suite exists

tradeoffs: **Content Addressing vs. Naming**: Hash-based identity decouples from names but couples to implementation details (changing algorithm changes identity)
**Distributed Transparency vs. Network Reality**: `Remote` abstracts distribution but couples logic to serialization constraints
**Immutability vs. Performance**: Persistent data structures couple performance to structure sharing discipline
**Ability Inference vs. Explicitness**: Type inference can hide effect requirements, coupling understanding to compiler
**Codebase Manager vs. Traditional VCS**: Git independence decouples from version control but couples to Unison tooling
verdict: Unison's content-addressed code and algebraic effects create exceptionally low forced coupling. Content addressing means functions are truly self-contained—no dependency on import paths, build order, or deployment infrastructure. Abilities provide better effect separation than Haskell's monolithic IO. Main weakness: immature ecosystem and learning curve for content-addressed paradigm.

energy.text: Compiles to native code: the fastest class in the language energy and time benchmarks [@pereira2017energy; @pereira2021ranking]. A causal re-analysis attributes the difference to execution time [@vankempen2025green].

ai-readiness.text: Sparse training data: models write it unreliably [@joel2025lowresource].

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path for safety-critical systems.

delivery.note: A definition's identity is its content hash, so code crosses by hash and not by binary
